rich_summary: As Ravana abducts Sita and carries her away, the aged vulture-king Jatayu awakens and confronts the demon king. Perched above them, Jatayu rebukes Ravana with a long moral warning, invoking dharma and the duties of kings. He reminds Ravana that Sita is the faithful wife of Rama, a righteous ruler whose wrath will be terrible. Jatayu denounces Ravana’s act as shameful, predicting that abducting Sita is like carrying a deadly serpent or wearing the noose of death. Though extremely old, he declares he will fight to protect her out of loyalty to Rama and King Dasaratha. The scene marks the first heroic resistance to the abduction, highlighting dharma, courage, and the coming clash between Ravana and Rama.

highlight_spans.why: Jatayu awakens and recognizes Ravana with Sita, establishing the divine witness who will challenge the abduction.
Jatayu proclaims Sita as Rama’s faithful consort and invokes Rama’s divine stature, framing the moral gravity of Ravana’s crime.
The vivid metaphor comparing Ravana’s act to carrying a venomous serpent or wearing the noose of death foreshadows his destruction.
The aged Jatayu declares he will risk his life to defend Sita for Rama’s sake, turning the confrontation into a moment of sacrificial heroism.
Jatayu openly challenges Ravana to stop and fight, transforming moral protest into the beginning of a mythic battle.

top_scenes.scene_text: The colossal vulture-king Jatayu perched on a towering tree spreads his wings and confronts Ravana’s chariot as the demon carries the struggling Sita through the forest sky.
Jatayu, ancient yet fierce, points his sharp mountain-like beak toward Ravana while delivering a thunderous warning as Sita watches with desperate hope.
Ravana’s ornate flying chariot races through the air with Sita in captivity while the giant bird Jatayu launches from a treetop to block its path.
